note: 'During the high priesthood of Abiathar, he entered the house of God and ate the consecrated bread' (Mark 2:26). **1 Samuel 21:1 names the priest as Ahimelech, Abiathar's father**, and the graph records the difference rather than resolving it: Mark says Abiathar, Samuel says Ahimelech, and both readings are old.

'Have you never read what David did when he and his companions were hungry and in need' (Mark 2:25), citing 1 Samuel 21:6 -- the Bread of the Presence eaten at Nob. Luke 6:3 tells it the same way. **The sabbath charge is answered with a precedent rather than a principle.**; 'The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.' (Matt 22:44), quoting Psalm 110:1 and turning it into a question about David: 'If then David calls him Lord, how is he his son?' (22:45).
'go and learn what this means: I desire mercy, not sacrifice.' (Matt 9:13), quoting Hosea 6:6. He sends them to look it up, which is unusual: **the answer is an instruction to go and read**.

'Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written: These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.' (Mark 7:6), quoting Isaiah 29:13. **He names the prophet**, which the gospels usually do not.

'Have you not read that from the beginning the Creator made them male and female ... For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife' (Matt 19:4-5), quoting Genesis 1:27 and 2:24 together.; 'This is the most important: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.' (Mark 12:29), quoting Deuteronomy 6:4-5 -- the Shema, and Mark keeps the opening line that Matthew 22:37 drops.; 'go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift prescribed by Moses, as a testimony to them' (Matt 8:4), pointing at Leviticus 14. **The cleansed leper is sent to the law**, and Luke 5:14 and Mark 1:44 tell it the same way.; 'For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother’ and ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’' (Mark 7:10), quoting Exodus 20:12 and 21:17 together -- **and using them against a tradition that let a man withhold support from his parents** (7:11-13).; 'What did Moses command you?' (Mark 10:3), and then the answer that goes behind it: 'Because of the hardness of your hearts he wrote you this commandment' (10:5). **He treats a Mosaic command as a concession rather than an ideal**, and reaches past it to Genesis.; 'Even Moses demonstrates that the dead are raised, in the passage about the burning bush. For he calls the Lord the God of Abraham' (Luke 20:37) -- Luke's version of the argument Matthew 22:32 makes, and Luke names the passage by its scene rather than its chapter.; 'If you had believed Moses, you would believe Me, because he wrote about Me.' (John 5:46). **The strongest claim any gospel makes about the relation between the two**, and it names no passage.; 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob' (Matt 22:32), quoting Exodus 3:6 -- the words from the bush -- and drawing the resurrection out of a tense: 'God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.'; 'Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind' (Matt 22:37), quoting Deuteronomy 6:5.; 'Love your neighbor as yourself.' (Matt 22:39), quoting Leviticus 19:18 -- **the second commandment he names comes out of the middle of the holiness code**, which is the part of Leviticus this graph has least of.; 'Even Moses demonstrates that the dead are raised, in the passage about the burning bush. For he calls the Lord the God of Abraham' (Luke 20:37), and Mark has 'have you not read in the book of Moses, in the account of the burning bush, how God told him' (12:26). **Both name the passage by its scene rather than by chapter** -- 'in the bush' is a citation, and the argument turns on the tense of what is said there.

'Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?' (Matt 9:11), answered 'It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick' (9:12).; 'Look, why are they doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?' (Mark 2:24), answered with David and the Bread of the Presence (2:25-26).; 'Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?' (Luke 6:2), answered with the same precedent Mark records (6:3-4).; 'Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders? Instead, they eat with defiled hands.' (Mark 7:5), answered out of Isaiah (7:6-7).; 'Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?' (Matt 19:3), asked 'to test Him', and answered from Genesis (19:4-5). **The exception clause at 19:9 is in Matthew and not in Mark or Luke**, which is the whole of the divorce argument.; 'When the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they themselves gathered together. One of them, an expert in the law, tested Him with a question' (Matt 22:34-35).

'Leave this place and get away, because Herod wants to kill You' (Luke 13:31), answered 'Go tell that fox' (13:32). **One of the few places Pharisees warn him rather than test him**, and the text does not say whether the warning was kindly meant.

'one of the scribes had come up and heard their debate. Noticing how well Jesus had answered them, he asked Him, Which commandment is the most important of all?' (Mark 12:28). **Mark's version is not hostile** -- the scribe asks because the previous answers were good, and at 12:34 Jesus tells him he is not far from the kingdom. Matthew 22:35 has a lawyer asking the same thing 'tempting him'.; "the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, He is possessed by Beelzebul"; 'Meanwhile, the chief priests and scribes stood there, vehemently accusing Him.' (Luke 23:10).
